context:
You questioned the retired-word list itself (item 49). An Opus reviewer read the glossary (14:57 CDT). Most retirements hold; three do not:
- claim became statement. The #780 lane made this swap with no ruling from you, and it reads "stating the statement".
- try became round. A build attempt is not a review round, and the glossary's round row contradicts itself.
- gap became debt. It merges the missing thing with its filed record, and "debt" reads as money.

Also: the list's "(prose)" tags dropped the plan's "(this sense)" qualifier, so correct text such as "GitHub issue" or "blockquote" gets flagged. A separate blind redo of the vocabulary, built without seeing the glossary, also chose "coordinator", plus park, remark and handle; its table is available on request.

options.gain: Plainer words, and no false flags.
options.how:
Restore the three old words, put "(this sense)" back, and run one prose lane for the leftovers.
Before: the three words are retired and correct text is flagged. After: they are plain words again and only the retired sense is flagged.
options.label: Bring back claim, try and gap
options.lose: One more lane, and a partial undo of #780.

options.how:
No change to the glossary or the check.
Before and after: the same.
options.label: Keep today's words
options.lose: The awkward prose and the false flags stay.

ref: o13 (one name per thing: the glossary), item 49's cross review, lane B PR #780
reply:
Answered, Oct 28 16:15 CDT: bring back claim, try and gap (a). One lane puts the three words back as plain words, restores the "(this sense)" qualifier, and fixes the leftover prose. It partly undoes #780.

Built, Oct 28 18:07 CDT (draft PR 792, reviewed, joins the next batch). Two things to know; no pick needed. (1) "(this sense)" still keeps your item 49 a reach into file paths, rule anchors and record slugs, so a new path such as docs/github-issue-notes.md is still refused; leaving that out reopened a safety hole in review. So "no false flags" holds for code names and prose, not for paths. (2) The rule anchors that lane B renamed (such as outcomes-tests-are-statements) stay renamed; claim, try and gap come back in prose only (claim 32 places, try 13, gap 4). If you want the anchors back too, that is a new lane.
title: Three retired words look like poor swaps: keep them or bring them back?
why: Three swaps read worse than the words they replaced, and false flags teach people to ignore the check.
